Handoff: three follow-up fixes for `entire repo clone` ref parsing, plus authoritative entiredb research that changes how one of them should be done. Please open a new PR against main.

## Context

PR #2185 (`paul/clone-et`, trail 1186) added `/et/<project>/<repo>` native clone refs and merged 2026-09-02T00:06Z. PR #2223 (`paul/clone-ref-findings`, commits 0083f834d + 55e69b893) then landed to address two review findings, and it fixed both correctly — dot-only `/gh/` refs keep the parser's reason, and `git@github.com:foo/bar` now says "pass GitHub mirrors as /gh/foo/bar". Current main is ee6d53f3d. Do not redo that work. Everything below is what #2223 left, all in `cmd/entire/cli/repo_clone.go`.

## Item 1 (the main one): the `/et/`-prefixed form still loses its reason

`invalidCloneRefError` (repo_clone.go, added in 0083f834d) got a `mirrorCloneRefPrefixRe = ^/?gh/` branch that keeps the mirror parser's reason for malformed `gh/` refs. There is no symmetric `^/?et/` branch, so a native ref that fails the charset check falls through to the generic shape list. Verified against a binary built from ee6d53f3d:

    /et/foo_bar/dogbark  ->  invalid <repo> "/et/foo_bar/dogbark": expected /et/<project>/<repo>, <project>/<repo>, /gh/<owner>/<repo>, or a full entire:// URL
    /et/paul/dog_bark    ->  (identical)
    /et/paul/            ->  (identical)

The user typed exactly `/et/<project>/<repo>` and is told to type `/et/<project>/<repo>`. That is the same self-contradiction #2223 set out to remove, reproduced on the other side. Add an `^/?et/` branch that names the actual rule, mirroring what `parseMirrorCloneRef` now does for owner/repo ("project: lowercase letters, digits, '-'; repo: also interior '.'"). Note the existing `gh/` branch produces the ref twice in one message (`invalid <repo> "/gh/entirehq/..": repo cannot be dot-only: /gh/entirehq/..`) — worth not copying that shape.

## Item 2: the native charsets are looser than the server's, and the doc comment misstates the rules

I read the authoritative source in ~/Work/entire/devenv/entiredb at 2b81a3557 — `core/resource/project_name.go`, function `normalizeName`, reached from `core/coreapi/repos.go:75` (the repo-create path the CLI hits) and `core/api/admin_handlers.go:1381`. The real rules:

| rule | project | repo |
|---|---|---|
| charset | lowercase a-z, 0-9, `-` | same plus interior `.` |
| length | 3–32 | 1–64 |
| leading/trailing `-` | banned | banned |
| leading/trailing `.` | n/a | banned |
| consecutive `..` | n/a | banned |
| raw ULID as a name | banned | banned |
| uppercase | rejected at create; `foldProjectName` lowercases for lookup | same |

Against the CLI's `nativeProjectRe = ^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$` and `nativeRepoRe = ^[A-Za-z0-9.-]+$`, three things are wrong in the permissive direction, so refs the server can never match become a control-plane round trip instead of a local shape error: leading/trailing `-`, leading/trailing `.`, and consecutive dots. `paul/..`, `paul/.foo`, `paul/foo.`, `paul/-x` all currently parse as native refs. The mirror side already has `gitHubDotOnlyRe` for exactly this class; the native side has no equivalent. Tighten both regexes to the server shape and fix the doc comment, which currently says the project charset is "letters, digits, '-'" without noting the lowercase-at-create/fold-at-lookup split or any of the edge-character rules.

Three things in that comment are CORRECT — please don't "fix" them:
- "3–32 chars server-side" for projects is right (`projectNameMinLen`/`projectNameMaxLen`), so the `gh`/`et` two-char guard is genuinely safe. They are not in `reserved_names.txt`; the length rule is what excludes them.
- Accepting uppercase in the CLI regex is right, because lookups fold case.
- `resolveRepoRef`'s ULID short-circuit is safe, because `LooksLikeRawULID` (core/model/id.go:28) is banned as a name at create time, so a 26-char Crockford string in the ref position is always an ID.

Also please correct one claim of mine if you see it referenced anywhere: I previously said the constraints "aren't in the contract" because `internal/coreapi/spec/core.openapi.json` has `CreateProjectInputBody.name` as minLength 1 / maxLength 100 with no pattern, and cited the live project `gh:mirrors:01KS00CRNX8HFG5PX19S2WH2F0` as a counter-example. Both were wrong. The OpenAPI schema is only the wire shape; the resource layer enforces the real rules. And `gh:mirrors:<ownerID>` is a deliberate system-namespace project (`MirrorsProjectNamePrefix`, core/resource/store.go:1452) that `CreateProject` refuses to mint because of the `:`, and that is looked up via `findProjectByExactName`, which skips the shape check on purpose. It is not a counter-example. Optional but nice: pin the resource-layer rules in the OpenAPI spec so the client isn't generated against a looser contract than the server enforces.

## Item 3: `.git` suffix on a native ref

`entire repo clone /et/paul/dogbark.git` parses (interior dot is legal), then fails at lookup with `no repo named "dogbark.git" in that project`, with no hint — even though the code comment on `resolveNativeCloneURL` already flags that the server strips `.git` for `/gh/` paths only, so a `/et/` path carrying it 404s.

The research says do NOT strip or reject it at parse time. `foo.git` is a legal server repo name under the rules above (interior dot, no leading/trailing dot, no `..`), so a repo could genuinely be called that, and silently stripping would clone the wrong thing. `entire-trails.el` is the doc's own example of a legitimate dotted repo name. The right fix is a hint on the lookup miss: when the name ends in `.git` and the lookup returns not-found, suggest retrying without the suffix. Same treatment is worth considering for the full `entire://` passthrough branch, which forwards a `/et/...` URL with `.git` straight to `git clone` and lets the server 404.

## Verification

Existing tests to extend: `TestParseNativeCloneRef` and `TestInvalidCloneRefError` in `cmd/entire/cli/repo_clone_test.go`. There is currently no case covering an `/et/`-prefixed ref that fails the charset check — that gap is why item 1 shipped. Add the dot/hyphen edge cases too.

Repo standard before commit is `mise run fmt && mise run lint && mise run test:ci`; treat fmt-then-lint as one sequence. On main today the clone tests pass and `mise run lint` reports 0 issues, so anything failing is yours. Two known-unrelated local failures on macOS: `TestCodexAppServerHooksList_*` (`/var` vs `/private/var`) and versioncheck tests misclassifying `/usr/local` as Homebrew.

Please reference trail 1186 and PR #2185/#2223 in the PR body so the lineage is traceable, and note in the body that item 2 tightens client-side validation against rules verified in entiredb `core/resource/project_name.go` rather than inferred. Repo convention: never hard-wrap prose in PR bodies, one paragraph per line.
</cross-session-message>

This is what it left behind.

## 1. An `/et/`-prefixed ref lost its reason

#2223 gave `invalidCloneRefError` a `^/?gh/` branch so a malformed mirror ref keeps the mirror parser's reason. There was no symmetric `^/?et/` branch, so a native ref that failed the charset check fell through to the generic shape list:

```
$ entire repo clone /et/foo_bar/dogbark
invalid <repo> "/et/foo_bar/dogbark": expected /et/<project>/<repo>, <project>/<repo>, /gh/<owner>/<repo>, or a full entire:// URL
```

The user typed exactly `/et/<project>/<repo>` and was told to type `/et/<project>/<repo>` — the same self-contradiction #2223 set out to remove, reproduced on the other side. `parseNativeCloneRef` now returns an error rather than a bool, `invalidCloneRefError` grows the `et/` branch, and the message names the rule that was broken:

```
invalid <repo> "/et/foo_bar/dogbark": project "foo_bar" must be 3-32 characters of letters, digits and '-', not starting or ending with '-'
invalid <repo> "/et/paul/dog_bark":   repo "dog_bark" must be 1-64 characters of letters, digits, '.' and '-', not starting or ending with '.' or '-', and with no consecutive dots
invalid <repo> "/et/paul":            expected /et/<project>/<repo> or <project>/<repo> (2 names, got 1)
```

Declaring a forge token is the whole test for showing a parser's reason. A bare two-segment ref (`paul/.foo`) still gets the shape list, deliberately: it declared nothing, so it is equally a mangled URL — `git@github.com:foo/bar` is itself just a bad "project" name under the shorthand grammar, which is exactly the case #2223 fixed. That boundary is now pinned by a test.

The reasons name the offending segment rather than repeating the whole ref, so they avoid the shape the `gh/` branch produces (`invalid <repo> "/gh/entirehq/..": repo cannot be dot-only: /gh/entirehq/..`). The `gh/` messages are unchanged.

## 2. The native name check was looser than the server

The client accepted `^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$` / `^[A-Za-z0-9.-]+$` and left everything else to the server, so `paul/..`, `paul/.foo`, `paul/foo.` and `paul/-x` all parsed as native refs and cost a control-plane round trip to be told the repo does not exist. This tightens both regexes to the shape the server actually enforces, verified in entiredb `core/resource/project_name.go` (`normalizeName`, reached from `core/coreapi/repos.go:75` — the repo-create path the CLI hits — and `core/api/admin_handlers.go:1381`) rather than inferred: projects are 3–32 chars of lowercase letters, digits and `-`; repos 1–64 with interior `.` also allowed; neither may start or end with `-` (or `.`); no consecutive dots; and a raw ULID is refused as a name.

Three things the old comment got right and this keeps. Uppercase is still accepted, because both lookups fold case — the project through `foldProjectName`, and the repo on `lower(repo_registry.name)` in `getRepoGroupByProjectAndFullName`. The 3-char project minimum is real (`projectNameMinLen`), which is what makes the `<project>/<repo>` shorthand unambiguous; encoding it directly replaces the hand-written `gh`/`et` forge-token guard with the rule that guard was standing in for, so `ab/dogbark` is now a local shape error too. And the `..`/edge-dot bans are the reason `entire-trails.el` stays legal while `paul/..` does not.

Consecutive dots are checked outside the regex because RE2 has no negative lookahead. Interior hyphen runs and a hyphen adjacent to a dot (`dog--bark`, `dog-.bark`) are names the server accepts, so they are pinned as accepted — a per-segment regex, the tempting simplification here, would refuse them.

## 3. A `.git` suffix on a native ref

`entire repo clone /et/paul/dogbark.git` parsed and then failed at lookup with `no repo named "dogbark.git" in that project` and no hint, even though the server strips `.git` for `/gh/` paths only.

It is deliberately not stripped or refused at parse time: `foo.git` is a legal server repo name under the rules above (interior dot, no trailing dot, no `..`) — the same shape as `entire-trails.el`, and indistinguishable from it in the ref — so stripping could clone a different repo than the one named. The advice is attached at the lookup miss instead, the first point where the suffix is provably the cause. `noRepoNamedErr` becomes a typed error so the clone path can recognise the miss with `errors.As` instead of matching its text; its message is unchanged.

```
no repo named "dogbark.git" in that project (run `entire repo list <project>` to see names, or pass a ULID); a native ref keeps the .git suffix (it is stripped for /gh/ paths only) — retry as /et/paul/dogbark
```

The full-`entire://`-URL branch performs no lookup of ours, so it gets the same advice as a hedged note on stderr after `git clone` fails, and only for an `/et/` path carrying the suffix — a failed clone is just as likely to be auth or the network, and git has already printed the real diagnosis above it.

## Two corrections to earlier claims about the server rules

The name constraints **are** part of the contract, and my earlier note saying they "aren't in the contract" was wrong on both of its grounds. `internal/coreapi/spec/core.openapi.json` having `CreateProjectInputBody.name` as minLength 1 / maxLength 100 with no pattern only describes the wire shape; the resource layer enforces the real rules underneath it. Pinning the resource-layer rules into the OpenAPI schema is still worth doing, so the generated client is not built against a looser contract than the server enforces — but it belongs in entiredb, not here: `core.openapi.json` is the pristine upstream spec, refreshed by curl-ing the running server (see `internal/coreapi/gen.go`), so a hand edit in this repo would be reverted by the next sync.

`resolveRepoRef`'s ULID short-circuit is safe in practice but not for quite the stated reason. The CLI's `looksLikeULID` accepts any 26 Crockford-base32 characters, while the server's `LooksLikeRawULID` (`core/model/id.go:28`) additionally requires the first character to be in `0`-`7`. A name like `REDACTED` is therefore a legal server repo name that the CLI misreads as an ID (verified against both predicates). If dots were banned outright, that regex would have no reason to exist.

Real examples: `socket.io`, `next.js`, `docs.rs`, and `.github` — which not only contains a dot but *starts* with one.

So the actual GitHub rules are narrower than "no dots":

- **Allowed:** alphanumerics, `-`, `_`, `.`. Other characters (spaces included) get silently replaced with `-`.
- **Rejected:** a name that is only dots, and a name **ending in `.git`**.

| | GitHub repo | Entire native repo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| interior dot | yes | yes |
| leading/trailing dot | yes (`.github`) | **no** |
| consecutive dots | yes (`a..b` is accepted) | **no** |
| underscore | yes | **no** |
| ends in `.git` | **no** | yes |

## What changed

**Both clone-ref parsers now trim the suffix before validating the name**, and the ordering is load-bearing in each: `.git` alone fails as an *empty* name rather than sneaking through as a dotted one, and `/gh/<owner>/..git` — which isn't dot-only as typed — becomes so once the suffix goes, so the existing dot-only guard catches it.

**The mirror side gets this for the first time.** This turned out to be a pre-existing bug I hadn't noticed until I tested it: `/gh/foo/bar.git` used to look up a repo GitHub cannot have, then tell you to onboard it as `entire repo mirror create github.com/foo/bar.git` — an impossible name. Now:

```
/gh/foo/bar.git  -> no mirror found for /gh/foo/bar; run 'entire repo mirror create github.com/foo/bar' to onboard it
/gh/foo/..git    -> invalid <repo>: repo cannot be dot-only
/gh/foo/.git     -> invalid <repo>: repo name is empty once the .git suffix is dropped
```

`parseGitHubURL` already accepted `(?:\.git)?` on the URL forms, so the `/gh/` shorthand was the odd one out.

**`repo create` now refuses a name ending in `.git`**, suggesting the trimmed form. This is the piece that makes the policy coherent rather than just lenient — the server *would* accept `web.git`, so without it the CLI could mint a repo it can then only address by ULID.

**The hint machinery is gone**, and with it the `errNoRepoNamed` sentinel that existed only to key it — `resolveref.go` is now byte-identical to `main` (verified: `git diff main -- resolveref.go` is empty). The `serveNativeRepo` fixture went back to its value signature too, since the nil-miss branch lost its only callers.

## The tradeoff, stated plainly

This is a deliberate client-side narrowing of what the server allows, not a claim the server agrees. I re-verified that the server really does keep the suffix on native paths — `CanonicaliseMirrorPath` passes non-`/gh/` paths through untouched, and `repos.go:161` stamps `/et/<project>/<name>` verbatim. So a native repo named `foo.git` remains creatable via the API or web, and is now unaddressable *by name* in the CLI. Escape hatches: its ULID, and a full `entire://` URL, which `clone` still forwards to git verbatim.

The upside is that the five-way inconsistency I reported earlier is now closed by *joining* the majority rather than by touching `gitremote`, `trail_cmd` and `experts_cmd` — `repo clone` was the sole holdout, so nothing else needed changing.

Still open and untouched: `IsSupportedForge` doesn't know `et`, so `trail --repo et/paul/dogbark` is rejected outright with a suggestion pointing at a github.com URL. That's noted in the PR body as a separate gap — happy to fix it next if you want it in this PR or its own.

Done — `a3d820a70`, PR body updated with it as item 4. Full `test:ci` green, lint 0 issues.

**Investigating it changed the fix.** The gap wasn't "the CLI wrongly rejects a valid forge" — it was two bugs sharing one wrong error message.

`IsSupportedForge` was backed by `forgeToHost`, a map of **upstream** git hosts to their ids. A native repo has no upstream host, so `et` was simply absent — and the two questions *"does this forge have a public host?"* and *"is this a forge token in an `entire://` path?"* had silently collapsed into one. `gitremote.pathForges` now owns `{gh, et}` separately, plus the placeholder spelling of the segments that follow, since a mirror is addressed by owner and a native repo by project. `forgeToHost` is untouched, so `CanonicalHost` still falls back to the cluster host for a native remote rather than inventing a forge host — pinned by a test, because that's the thing a careless widening would break.

That fixed a second bug I hadn't reported: `git clone entire://et/paul/dogbark` was dying on `lookup et: no such host`, because the forge-id-in-the-host-slot check didn't recognize `et`. It now gets the same actionable message `gh` always got, with correct labels:

```
fatal: entire:// URL is missing its cluster host ("et" is a forge id, not a host).
The full form is entire://<cluster-host>/et/<project>/<repo>.
To clone it, run:

    entire repo clone /et/paul/dogbark
```

**But trails still refuse native refs — deliberately.** I checked entire-api before widening, and it's the decisive constraint: `validTrailsHosts` admits `{gh, et}`, but `resolvableTrailsHosts` is `{gh}` alone, with an explicit comment that `full_name` rows carry no forge host so *"et fails closed into the collapsed 404 … extend resolution deliberately then, don't widen this set."*

So accepting `et` would have traded a clear local error for an opaque server 404 — indistinguishable from permission-denied, by design. Instead the rejection stays and tells the truth:

```
invalid --repo "et/paul/dogbark": trails are not available for Entire-native repos yet;
pass a GitHub mirror as gh/<owner>/<repo> or a github.com clone URL
```

It now also catches the **URL** spelling (`--repo entire://host/et/p/r`), which previously slipped past the forge check straight into that 404 — a third thing that was broken and unreported.

One judgment call worth your eye: that check encodes client-side knowledge of a server-side gate, the same maintenance trap I flagged for the name rules. I've commented it to come out when entire-api gains forge-scoped naming, and documented the pairing in CLAUDE.md, but it will go stale silently if nobody looks. The alternative — let it through and eat the 404 — is honest but useless to the user, so I picked the informative one and flagged it.

Also: `missingClusterHostMessage` lost its "To pick a mirror interactively" line in favour of a neutral "To clone it, run:". The old wording was accurate for `gh` and wrong for `et`, and `repo clone` explains the picker itself when it prompts. Say the word if you'd rather keep the per-forge phrasing.

Confirmed both details. Here's the resulting behavior.

## The grammar becomes prefix-determined

Today the first segment is *ambiguous*: two segments meant native, three meant forge-prefixed. After integrating #2252, **the leading token alone decides which grammar is tried** — `et/` → native, `gh/` → mirror, `entire://` → passthrough, anything else → nothing. Leading slash stays optional on the two ref forms.

That's the whole conceptual shift, and it makes my item-1 dispatch exact rather than heuristic: "did the ref declare this parser's token" *is* the parser's own first check.

## Behavior table

| input | outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `/et/paul/dogbark`, `et/paul/dogbark` | ✅ clones the native repo from its home cluster |
| `/gh/acme/app`, `gh/acme/app` | ✅ clones the mirror (cluster picker if multi-placement) |
| `entire://host/et/p/r`, `entire://host/gh/o/r` | ✅ forwarded to `git clone` verbatim |
| `/et/paul/dogbark.git`, `/gh/acme/app.git` | ✅ suffix dropped → `dogbark` / `app` |
| `/et/foo_bar/dogbark` | ❌ `project "foo_bar" must be 3-32 characters of letters, digits and '-'…` |
| `/et/paul/dog_bark` | ❌ `repo "dog_bark" must be 1-64 characters…` |
| `/et/ab/dogbark` | ❌ same project rule — **locally**, no control-plane round trip |
| `/et/paul`, `/et/`, `/et/p/r/extra` | ❌ `expected /et/<project>/<repo>…` with the segment count |
| `/gh/foo_bar/baz`, `/gh/acme` | ❌ the mirror parser's reason (unchanged) |
| **`paul/dogbark`** | ❌ **shape list** — this is the behavior change |
| `dogbark`, `/gl/foo/bar`, `//et/p/r` | ❌ shape list |
| `git@github.com:acme/app`, `https://github.com/acme/app` | ❌ but hinted: `pass GitHub mirrors as /gh/acme/app` |
| `github.com/acme/app` | ❌ shape list, **no hint** — see below |
| `entire://et/p/r` (token in the host slot) | ❌ but `git-remote-entire` gives the actionable message (my item 4) |

The shape list itself shortens to `/et/<project>/<repo>, /gh/<owner>/<repo>, or a full entire:// URL`.

The one category that *disappears* is "looks like a shorthand but has a bad name" — what `paul/.foo` used to be. Every rejected ref now either declares a token and gets a precise reason, or declares none and gets the list.

## What I'd delete as obsolete

The 3-char project minimum stops being load-bearing. Right now my code and CLAUDE.md justify it as *what makes the shorthand unambiguous* — that's why I could delete the old explicit `gh`/`et` guard, and it's what `TestForgeTokensCannotBeProjectNames` pins. With the token mandatory, none of that reasoning holds. The minimum stays (server parity, still saves a round trip on `/et/ab/x`), but I'd drop that test and rewrite the justification, plus two comments that mention the shorthand. Leaving them would assert a rationale the grammar no longer has, which is worse than saying nothing.

## One deliberate non-change

`declaresForge` becomes redundant *in principle* — the parsers now key on the same leading token. The altitude review's suggested fix (parsers return a "not my grammar" sentinel; the dispatcher shows the first real reason) would delete it. I'd still keep it, because `explain_repo.go:111` wraps `parseMirrorCloneRef`'s error with `%w` and renders it verbatim to `explain --repo` users, so turning that into a sentinel changes an unrelated command's message. Two grammars doesn't pay for that yet.

## Two things #2252 newly unlocks — your call

**(a) `github.com/acme/app` could get the `/gh/` hint.** It currently falls to the shape list, which doesn't mention GitHub at all. The blocker was that `gitHubBareRe`'s `github.com/` prefix is *optional*, so admitting it would also match a bare `foo/bar` and answer a would-be native shorthand with "pass GitHub mirrors as /gh/foo/bar" — precisely the trap #2223 closed. A new regex requiring the literal `github.com/` prefix fixes that cleanly. Small, clearly an improvement.

**(b) A bare two-segment ref could name both candidates** — `paul/dogbark` → *"did you mean `/et/paul/dogbark` or `/gh/paul/dogbark`?"* instead of the generic list. This is exactly what people typed before, so it's the input that'll sting; naming both is honest (no guessing which they meant) and actionable. I'd recommend this one, but it is a product-flavoured choice on someone else's revert, so I'm not folding it in unasked.

Want me to integrate #2252 plain, or with (a), (b), or both? Also worth deciding: keep the commit attributed to toothbrush's change in the message, and note on #2252 that it's been absorbed here so it can be closed rather than rebased.

repo clone: require the forge prefix on every ref

Integrates #2252 (thanks @toothbrush) and builds two things on top of it.

The bare `<project>/<repo>` shorthand is gone; a native ref names its
`et/` token, so the leading token alone decides which grammar is tried.
`<owner>/<repo>` and `<project>/<repo>` are the same shape, so any default
would let one namespace shadow the other — register `acme/tool` in
whichever namespace the CLI prefers and a ref the user believes names the
other one silently resolves, then gets cloned and run. There is no safe
default, so there is none.

TestCloneRefAlwaysRequiresItsForgePrefix pins that at every layer rather
than just in the parser a refactor might route around: neither grammar
accepts a bare pair, the command refuses one without reaching the control
plane or `git clone`, and an ambiguous pair is never resolved to one forge.
Verified it fails on a reintroduced shorthand — and that the command-level
assertion is the one that catches it, since the bare ref then reaches the
network instead of erroring at the parse.

Two things the mandatory token unlocks:

- a bare pair now gets the forge-qualified refs it could have meant, one
  per grammar that would actually accept it, instead of the whole shape
  list. `paul/dogbark` offers both; `paul/dog_bark` and `ab/dogbark` offer
  only `/gh/`, since neither can be a native name. bareRefSuggestions
  re-runs the parsers rather than re-deriving their charsets, so a
  suggestion is never a ref that fails next.
- `github.com/acme/app` gets the `/gh/` hint it used to miss.
  parseHostedGitHubURL can now take the host-qualified bare form, because
  the shape it had to stay away from — an unqualified pair — is no longer
  a native ref. It still refuses the unqualified form: that would be the
  same namesquatting guess in a different place.

that the 3-char project minimum is load-bearing. It was what made the
shorthand unambiguous; with the token mandatory the bounds are server
parity only, and what they still buy is a local error instead of a round
trip. Merged main in for the #2185 changelog entry this amends.
